New Zealand will be buoyed with the way they have bounced back with the ball. The pacers bowled good lines and lengths and picked up wickets at regular intervals after the 137-ball stand between Ali and Babar provided some resistance. They will hope to restrict Pakistan to a moderate total and chase it down. So despite a day lost to rain, we might have a result inside four days. That's all from us for today. Do join us tomorrow at 0300 IST for all the action from Day 4. Please remember - DUE TO NO TELEVISION FEED, THERE WON'T BE ANY COMMENTARY. Until then, it's goodbye and take care!

Pakistan though came out with an ultra-defensive mindset. Having played a lot of shots in the first innings they went into a shell this time around. It did not work as the pressure began to tell and Pakistan are now struggling with a lead of just 62 and have only three wickets in hand. Azhar Ali consumed 173 balls for his 31 and his approach put some unnecessary pressure on the rest of the batting. Asad Shafiq is still out there and Pakistan will hope he can shepherd the tail to get any lead of over 150 for them to have a chance.

That's STUMPS on Day 3! Ends another entertaining day of Test cricket. New Zealand began the day looking to post a big score but Pakistan came back roaring in the game to bundle them out for 200. Rahat Ali was the star with a 4-wicket haul. Amir and Sohail Khan chipped in with three wickets each. New Zealand got a slender lead of 67 runs but made the most of it.
